entities.name: What Is Agiorgitiko?
entities.description: Learn what Agiorgitiko is, where it comes from, how it tastes and why Greek examples can range from fresh, soft-tannined reds to fuller, oak-aged wines.

entities.name: What is Albariño?
entities.description: Albariño is a white grape variety known for fresh, aromatic wines with noticeable acidity. Learn about its names, origins, Australian context, taste and food pairings.

entities.name: What Is Aligoté?
entities.description: Learn what Aligoté is, where it is grown, what it tastes like and how it differs from Chardonnay, including useful context for Australian wine learners.

entities.name: What Is Arneis?
entities.description: Arneis is a dry, fragrant white grape from Piedmont. Learn its typical flavours, Roero connection, Australian presence and label meaning.

entities.name: What Is Assyrtiko?
entities.description: Learn what Assyrtiko is, where it comes from, how its dry white wines taste and why Australian drinkers may encounter this Greek grape.

entities.name: What Is Barbera?
entities.description: Learn what Barbera is, what its wines taste like, why acidity defines the grape, how it differs from Nebbiolo and where it is grown in Australia.

entities.name: What is Cabernet Franc?
entities.description: Cabernet Franc is a red wine grape known for red fruit, freshness and herbal or floral character. Learn how it differs from Cabernet Sauvignon and is used in Australian wine.

entities.name: Cabernet Sauvignon vs Cabernet Franc
entities.description: Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc are related but distinct grapes. Compare their flavour, body, tannin, acidity, blending roles and Australian context.

entities.name: What Is Carignan?
entities.description: Learn what Carignan is, where it comes from, what it tastes like, how it is grown and where Australian drinkers may encounter this Mediterranean red grape.

entities.name: What Is Carménère?
entities.description: Learn what Carménère is, why it is associated with Chile, how its wines can taste and what Australian wine learners should know about this distinctive red grape.

entities.name: Chablis and Chardonnay
entities.description: Chablis is made from Chardonnay, but it is not another name for the grape. Learn how place, appellation, label wording and wine style fit together.

entities.name: Champagne vs English sparkling wine
entities.description: Champagne and English sparkling wine can share grapes and the traditional method, but their protected origins, rules, climates and styles differ. Here’s what Australian wine learners need to know.

entities.name: What is Chenin Blanc?
entities.description: Chenin Blanc is a versatile white wine grape that can produce dry, off-dry, sweet and sparkling wines. Learn its flavours, acidity, Australian context and food-pairing styles.

entities.name: Chenin Blanc vs Sauvignon Blanc
entities.description: Understand the difference between Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Blanc, including aroma, acidity, texture, sweetness, style range and Australian examples.

entities.name: What Is Cinsault?
entities.description: Cinsault, also written Cinsaut, is a soft, fruity red wine grape used for red wines, blends and rosé. Learn its taste, origins and Australian context.

entities.name: What Is Corvina?
entities.description: Corvina is an Italian red wine grape associated with Veneto, Verona and Valpolicella. Learn its flavour profile, Australian context and relationship to Amarone and Recioto.

entities.name: What Is Dolcetto?
entities.description: Learn what Dolcetto is, where it comes from, how its dry, fruity and bitter-almond style tastes, and what Australian drinkers should know.

entities.name: What Is Durif?
entities.description: Durif is a dark-skinned red Vitis vinifera grape variety. It originated in France and is documented as the offspring of Syrah and Peloursin.

entities.name: What is Fiano?
entities.description: Fiano is a white wine grape that can make fresh, citrus-led or fuller, textural wines. Learn what Fiano tastes like, where it is grown in Australia and how to read it on a label.

entities.name: What Is Furmint?
entities.description: Furmint is a Hungarian white wine grape that can make both dry and sweet wines. Learn how Tokaj, harvest timing, botrytis and residual sugar shape its style.

entities.name: What is Gamay?
entities.description: Gamay is a red wine grape best known from Beaujolais. Learn its typical flavours, structure, Australian context, serving guidance and the role of carbonic maceration.

entities.name: What Is Garganega?
entities.description: Learn what Garganega is, where it comes from, how it relates to Soave and what its wines can taste like—including useful context for Australian wine learners.

entities.name: What Is Gewürztraminer?
entities.description: Learn what Gewürztraminer is, how its floral and lychee aromas differ from sweetness, where it is grown in Australia and how to serve and pair it.

entities.name: What Is Glera?
entities.description: Learn what Glera is, why it is associated with Prosecco, how Glera wines typically taste, and what Australian drinkers should understand about the label.

entities.name: Grenache vs Pinot Noir
entities.description: Grenache vs Pinot Noir explained for Australian wine learners: compare body, acidity, tannin, fruit character, texture, Australian regions and food pairing.

entities.name: What Is Grüner Veltliner?
entities.description: Learn what Grüner Veltliner is, where it comes from, how its dry, fresh and peppery styles taste, and what Australian wine drinkers should know.

entities.name: What Is Lagrein?
entities.description: Learn what Lagrein is, where it comes from, how red and rosé expressions differ, what it may taste like and what Australian wine learners should expect from the label.

entities.name: What is Malbec?
entities.description: Malbec is a red wine grape known for deeply coloured, dry reds with dark-fruit and violet flavours. Learn how Argentina, Cahors and Australia shape its style.

entities.name: Malbec vs Cabernet Sauvignon
entities.description: Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon compared: learn how their fruit, tannin, body, acidity and Australian expressions commonly differ.

entities.name: Malbec vs Shiraz
entities.description: Malbec and Shiraz are different red grape varieties. Learn how their typical flavours, structure, Australian styles, labels and food pairings compare.

entities.name: What Is Marsanne?
entities.description: Marsanne is a northern Rhône white grape that makes dry, textured wines and has a small but established Australian history. Learn its flavours, styles and difference from Roussanne.

entities.name: What is Mataro / Mourvèdre?
entities.description: Mataro, Mourvèdre and Monastrell are names for the same red wine grape. Learn how the grape tastes, why it matters in Australian wine and how to read its name on a label.

entities.name: What Is Melon de Bourgogne?
entities.description: Learn what Melon de Bourgogne is, how it relates to Muscadet, what its wines typically taste like, what “sur lie” means and how Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What Is Mencía?
entities.description: Mencía is a red grape from north-western Spain. Learn where it is grown, what Mencía wine tastes like and how its style varies, including its emerging Australian context.

entities.name: Merlot vs Pinot Noir
entities.description: Understand the typical differences between Merlot and Pinot Noir, including body, acidity, tannin, flavour, Australian regional context and practical choosing tips.

entities.name: What Is Montepulciano?
entities.description: Learn what Montepulciano is, how it differs from Montepulciano d’Abruzzo and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, what its wines can taste like, and how Australian drinkers may encounter the grape.

entities.name: What is Moscato / Muscat?
entities.description: Learn what Moscato and Muscat mean, how the names differ, and why these aromatic grapes can produce dry, sweet, still, sparkling and fortified wines in Australia.

entities.name: Moscato vs Riesling
entities.description: Understand the difference between Moscato and Riesling, including sweetness, acidity, aroma, Australian styles, label clues and food-pairing starting points.

entities.name: Nebbiolo vs Pinot Noir
entities.description: Nebbiolo is usually firmer and more tannic, while Pinot Noir is generally more delicate, perfumed and supple. Learn how structure, aroma, Australian region and food pairing shape the comparison.

entities.name: Nebbiolo vs Sangiovese
entities.description: Nebbiolo and Sangiovese are distinct Italian red grapes. Compare their colour, acidity, tannin, body, aromas, food suitability and Australian expressions.

entities.name: What Is Nero d’Avola?
entities.description: Nero d’Avola is a Sicilian red wine grape that can make fresh, fruity or fuller, structured dry wines. Learn its taste, structure, Australian context and serving ideas.

entities.name: What Is Petit Verdot?
entities.description: Learn what Petit Verdot is, how it tastes, why it is used in blends, how it differs from Petite Sirah and where it fits in Australian wine.

entities.name: What Is Petite Sirah?
entities.description: Learn what Petite Sirah is, how it relates to Durif, what the wine commonly tastes like, and why Australian labels usually use the name Durif.

entities.name: What Is Picpoul?
entities.description: Picpoul is a fresh, high-acid white grape best known in southern France. Learn its names, flavours, Picpoul de Pinet connection and Australian context.

entities.name: What Is Pinot Blanc?
entities.description: Pinot Blanc is a fresh, pale white wine grape related to Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris. Learn its names, flavours, styles, Australian context and food pairings.

entities.name: Pinot Gris vs Pinot Grigio
entities.description: Pinot Gris and Pinot Grigio are names for the same grape. Learn how regional traditions can suggest different styles, why Australian examples overlap, and how to choose a bottle.

entities.name: What Is Pinot Meunier?
entities.description: Pinot Meunier is a distinct grape closely related to Pinot Noir and best known for its role in traditional-method sparkling wine. Learn what it tastes like, how it is used and what Australian labels may call it.

entities.name: Pinot Noir vs Gamay
entities.description: Pinot Noir and Gamay are different grapes that can make fresh, lighter-bodied reds. Compare their fruit, structure, winemaking influences, Australian context, food matches and serving cues.

entities.name: Prosecco vs pét-nat
entities.description: Prosecco and pét-nat are not the same thing. Learn how their origins, grapes, fermentation methods, sweetness, bubbles and sediment can differ.

entities.name: Riesling vs Gewürztraminer
entities.description: Riesling and Gewürztraminer are different aromatic white grapes. Learn how they differ in aroma, acidity, body and sweetness, with Australian context.

entities.name: What Is Roussanne?
entities.description: Roussanne is a Rhône white grape that can make floral, textured and complex wines. Learn how it differs from Marsanne and where Australians may encounter it.

entities.name: What Is Sagrantino?
entities.description: Sagrantino is an Italian red grape known for deep colour, firm tannin and fresh structure. Learn the difference between dry Secco and sweet Passito, plus what Australian drinkers can expect.

entities.name: Sauvignon Blanc vs Sémillon
entities.description: Understand the difference between Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, including aroma, acidity, texture, ageing, Hunter Valley Sémillon and Australian blends.

entities.name: What Is Savagnin?
entities.description: Learn what Savagnin is, how it differs from Sauvignon Blanc and Albariño, why it is associated with Jura, and what its Australian history means for wine drinkers.

entities.name: What Is Sémillon?
entities.description: Sémillon is a versatile white wine grape that can produce fresh, dry, sweet, rich and bottle-aged wines. Learn its Australian expressions, Hunter Valley style and relationship with Sauvignon Blanc.

entities.name: Shiraz vs Grenache
entities.description: Understand the practical differences between Shiraz and Grenache, including flavour, body, tannin, Australian regions, blends and food-friendly styles.

entities.name: Syrah vs Shiraz
entities.description: Syrah and Shiraz are generally names for the same grape. Learn why the names differ, what Australian labels mean and how climate and winemaking shape the style.

entities.name: What Is Tannat?
entities.description: Learn what Tannat is, where it comes from, what it tastes like, why it can feel tannic, and how Australian drinkers may encounter this distinctive red grape.

entities.name: Tempranillo vs Sangiovese
entities.description: Tempranillo and Sangiovese are different red grapes. Compare their acidity, tannin, fruit, oak, food pairing and Australian wine styles.

entities.name: What Is Torrontés?
entities.description: Torrontés is an aromatic white grape best known from Argentina. Learn about its three varieties, floral flavours, dry style, Australian presence and food pairings.

entities.name: What Is Touriga Nacional?
entities.description: Learn what Touriga Nacional is, how it differs from Port, what it can taste like, and where Australian drinkers may encounter this Portuguese grape variety.

entities.name: What Is Trebbiano?
entities.description: Trebbiano is a family of white grape names, not always one single variety. Learn how Trebbiano Toscano relates to Ugni Blanc, why Trebbiano wines vary and how Australian drinkers may encounter the name.

entities.name: What Is Verdelho?
entities.description: Learn what Verdelho is, how it tastes, whether it is sweet or dry, and why this Portuguese-associated white grape matters in Australian wine.

entities.name: What Is Verdicchio?
entities.description: Learn what Verdicchio is, where it comes from, how it tastes and how to read Verdicchio labels in Australia.

entities.name: What Is Vermentino?
entities.description: Vermentino is a fresh, flexible white grape that makes dry wines ranging from crisp and citrus-led to broad and textural. Learn its names, flavours, origins and Australian context.

entities.name: Vermentino vs Sauvignon Blanc
entities.description: Vermentino and Sauvignon Blanc can both make dry white wines, but their typical aromas, texture and Australian context differ. Learn what to expect.

entities.name: What Is Viognier?
entities.description: Learn what Viognier is, what it tastes like, whether it is sweet and how Australian Viognier can vary in style.

entities.name: What is Aglianico?
entities.description: A beginner-friendly guide to Aglianico: the southern Italian red grape, its tannin and acidity, Taurasi and Aglianico del Vulture, Australian examples and food pairing.

entities.name: What is Alicante Bouschet?
entities.description: Discover what Alicante Bouschet is, why it is known as a teinturier grape, what styles it can produce and where it is grown in Australia.

entities.name: What is Arinto?
entities.description: Arinto is a Portuguese white wine grape known for high acidity, freshness and citrus-like character. Learn where it is used and how its wines can vary.

entities.name: What is Baga?
entities.description: Baga is a Portuguese red wine grape best known from Bairrada. Learn where it grows, how Baga wines can taste and how to recognise the name on a label.

entities.name: What is Blaufränkisch?
entities.description: Blaufränkisch is a Central European red grape variety known for berry fruit, fresh acidity, spice and tannin. Learn its names, style and Australian label context.

entities.name: What is Bonarda?
entities.description: Bonarda is usually Argentina’s name for Corbeau, a dark-fruited red grape with a useful freshness. Learn how its identity, style, regions and label meaning vary.

entities.name: What is Bourboulenc?
entities.description: Bourboulenc is an old southern French white wine grape that can bring freshness, acidity, floral and fruit character to varietal wines and blends. Learn where it is used, how it may taste and how Australian drinkers might encounter it.

entities.name: What is Brachetto?
entities.description: Brachetto is an aromatic Italian grape best known for sweet, fragrant wines from Piemonte. Learn how the grape differs from Brachetto d’Acqui DOCG, what styles to expect and how to serve it.

entities.name: What Is Cabernet Sauvignon?
entities.description: Cabernet Sauvignon is a structured red grape known for dark fruit, acidity and firm tannin. Learn how its style varies and where it thrives in Australia.

entities.name: What is Carricante?
entities.description: Carricante is a Sicilian white grape best known for Etna wines. Learn about its acidity, flavours, label terms, food matches and emerging Australian context.

entities.name: What is Catarratto?
entities.description: Catarratto is a Sicilian white wine grape that can make fresh, dry whites or fuller blends. Learn what the name means, how the style varies and how Australians may encounter it.

entities.name: What is Cesanese?
entities.description: Cesanese is a Lazio-associated Italian red-grape family. Learn what the name means, how Cesanese varieties differ, what the wines can taste like and how to approach a bottle in Australia.

entities.name: What Is Chardonnay?
entities.description: Chardonnay is a versatile white wine grape that can make fresh, citrusy, oaky, creamy, still or sparkling wines. Learn what it tastes like and why styles vary.

entities.name: What is Cortese?
entities.description: Cortese is a white Italian grape best known in Piedmont’s Gavi area. Learn how Cortese tastes and why not every Cortese wine is Gavi.

entities.name: What is Counoise?
entities.description: Counoise is a southern Rhône red-wine grape best known for adding freshness, fruit and spice to blends. Learn its style, uses and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Duras?
entities.description: Duras is a red grape from south-west France, best known in Gaillac. Learn about its peppery, fresh style—and why it is not the same as Durif.

entities.name: What is Encruzado?
entities.description: Encruzado is a Portuguese white wine grape, especially associated with Dão. Learn how its wines can combine freshness, acidity, body and texture, and why styles vary.

entities.name: What is Falanghina?
entities.description: Falanghina is a southern Italian white grape associated with Campania. Learn its typical flavours, styles, serving temperature and food-pairing starting points.

entities.name: What is Fer Servadou?
entities.description: Fer Servadou is a south-west French red wine grape known also as Fer N, Braucol and Mansois. Learn where it grows, how its wines taste and how to recognise the name.

entities.name: What is Frappato?
entities.description: Frappato is a Sicilian red grape variety known for fragrant, fresh and relatively gentle red wines. Learn how it relates to Cerasuolo di Vittoria and Nero d’Avola.

entities.name: What is Godello?
entities.description: Godello is a white grape variety from north-west Spain, especially associated with Galicia’s Valdeorras appellation. Learn about its typical style, regional identity and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Greco?
entities.description: Greco is a white Italian wine grape associated with Campania and Greco di Tufo. Learn the difference between the grape, the appellation and similar names.

entities.name: What Is Grenache?
entities.description: Grenache is a versatile red grape known for red fruit, spice and warmth. Learn about its Australian styles, blends and growing regions.

entities.name: What is Grillo?
entities.description: Grillo is an Italian white wine grape strongly associated with Sicily. Learn what Grillo tastes like, how its style varies and how to read the label.

entities.name: What is Hondarrabi Zuri?
entities.description: Hondarrabi Zuri is a Basque white wine grape best known through Txakoli. Learn how the grape, regional wine names and protected designations differ, plus what to expect in the glass.

entities.name: What is Inzolia?
entities.description: Inzolia is an Italian white wine grape associated with Sicily. Learn its other names, typical wine style, Australian context and how to serve it.

entities.name: What is Jacquère?
entities.description: Jacquère is a white grape associated with Savoie in the French Alps, typically producing light, fresh, lively white wines.

entities.name: What is Kerner?
entities.description: Kerner is a German white wine grape related to Riesling. Learn how Kerner tastes, whether it is sweet, where it is grown and how it differs from Riesling.

entities.name: What is Listán Negro?
entities.description: Learn what Listán Negro is, where it is grown, how its wines can taste and how to understand the grape name on a label.

entities.name: What is Loureiro?
entities.description: Loureiro is a Portuguese white wine grape associated with Vinho Verde. Learn what Loureiro wines typically taste like, how the grape is used and how Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What is Malvasia?
entities.description: Malvasia is a name used for several grape varieties and wine styles. Learn how dry, sweet and fortified Malvasia wines differ, and how to read the label.

entities.name: What is Mavrodaphne?
entities.description: Mavrodaphne is a Greek red grape best known for sweet, often fortified wines from Patras and Cephalonia. Learn how the name works on a wine label.

entities.name: What is Mazuelo?
entities.description: Mazuelo is a red wine grape also known as Carignan. Learn where it comes from, how it tastes, why it is used in blends and what Australian drinkers may find on a label.

entities.name: What Is Merlot?
entities.description: Merlot is a red grape known for plum and dark-fruit flavours, moderate tannin and a smooth texture. Learn how its styles vary.

entities.name: What is Mondeuse?
entities.description: Mondeuse is a black-skinned French grape, usually Mondeuse noire, known for deeply coloured, aromatic red wines with lively acidity and firm tannin. Learn its naming history, style and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Monica?
entities.description: Monica is a red wine grape associated with Sardinia. Learn what Monica N. tastes like, how it differs from Monica di Sardegna and how Australian readers may encounter it.

entities.name: What Is Nebbiolo?
entities.description: Nebbiolo is a pale-coloured but structured red grape known for high acidity, firm tannin and complex aromas. Learn how to approach it.

entities.name: What is Negroamaro?
entities.description: Negroamaro is a dark-skinned Italian wine grape associated with Puglia and Salento. Learn what its wines taste like, how styles vary, what the label names mean and why Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What is Nerello Mascalese?
entities.description: Nerello Mascalese is a Sicilian red grape best known from Mount Etna. Learn about its flavour, acidity, tannin, regional identity, food pairings and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Nosiola?
entities.description: Nosiola is a white wine grape associated with Trentino, Italy. Learn what dry Nosiola tastes like, how it differs from Vino Santo Trentino and where Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What is País?
entities.description: País is a historic red wine grape associated with Chile. Learn about its identity, history, synonyms and the varied styles of wine it can produce.

entities.name: What is Pallagrello Nero?
entities.description: Pallagrello Nero is a Campanian red-wine grape associated with Caserta. Learn what it tastes like, how it differs from Pallagrello Bianco and what its name means on a label.

entities.name: What is Pecorino wine grape?
entities.description: Pecorino is an Italian white wine grape known for fresh acidity, texture and floral, fruit, spice and almond-like characters. Learn where it comes from, what it tastes like and how it is grown in Australia.

entities.name: What is Picolit?
entities.description: Picolit is a white grape variety best known for concentrated, often sweet wines from Friuli. Learn about its identity, styles, flavours and small Australian presence.

entities.name: What Is Pinot Gris / Pinot Grigio?
entities.description: Pinot Gris and Pinot Grigio are names for the same grape. Learn why both appear on labels, how the styles can differ and what Australian drinkers should look for.

entities.name: What Is Pinot Noir?
entities.description: Pinot Noir is a red grape variety known for fresh acidity, red-fruit flavours and often lighter to medium-bodied wines. Learn what it tastes like, whether it is sweet and where it is grown in Australia.

entities.name: What is Poulsard?
entities.description: Poulsard is a Jura-associated red grape that often makes pale, fresh, red-fruited wines. Learn about Ploussard, colour, style and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Prie Blanc?
entities.description: Prié blanc is a high-altitude white wine grape from Valle d’Aosta. Learn its names, regional identity, typical fresh style and how it may appear on labels.

entities.name: What is Rabigato?
entities.description: Rabigato is a Portuguese white wine grape especially associated with the Douro. Learn how it tastes, how it is used in blends and how Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What is Refosco?
entities.description: Refosco is a name associated with several dark-skinned grape varieties from north-eastern Italy. Learn why Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso matters, what these wines may taste like and how to read the label.

entities.name: What is Ribolla Gialla?
entities.description: Ribolla Gialla is a fresh, high-acid white grape from north-eastern Italy and nearby Slovenia. Learn its typical flavours, styles and Australian context.

entities.name: What Is Riesling?
entities.description: Riesling is an aromatic white grape that can make dry, off-dry and sweet wines. Learn how acidity, fruitiness and Australian regions shape its style.

entities.name: What is Roditis?
entities.description: Roditis is a pink-skinned Greek wine grape usually made into fresh, dry white wine. Learn about its taste, style, names, origins and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Romorantin?
entities.description: Romorantin is a rare French white wine grape best known from the Loire Valley appellation of Cour-Cheverny. Learn its identity, style, history and Australian context.

entities.name: What is Rossese?
entities.description: Rossese is a wine-grape name associated especially with red wines from Liguria. Learn how Rossese differs from Rossese di Dolceacqua, what the wines can taste like and how to read the label.

entities.name: What is Rotgipfler?
entities.description: Rotgipfler is an Austrian white wine grape associated with the Thermenregion. Learn what it tastes like, how it differs from Zierfandler and how to serve it.

entities.name: What is Ruchè?
entities.description: Ruchè is a Piedmont red grape known for dry, aromatic, medium-bodied wines. Learn the difference between the grape and Ruchè di Castagnole Monferrato DOCG.

entities.name: What Is Sangiovese?
entities.description: Sangiovese is an Italian red grape known for bright acidity, savoury character and red-fruit flavours. Learn what to expect in Australian examples.

entities.name: What is Saperavi?
entities.description: Saperavi is a Georgian red wine grape known for deeply coloured, structured wines. Learn what it tastes like, how it is made and why Australians may encounter it.

entities.name: What Is Sauvignon Blanc?
entities.description: Sauvignon Blanc is a fresh, aromatic white wine grape variety. Learn what it tastes like, whether it is sweet and how Australian styles vary.

entities.name: What is Schiava?
entities.description: Schiava is a red grape best known in Alto Adige. Learn about its names, typical fresh and floral style, regional labels and what Australian drinkers may encounter.

entities.name: What Is Shiraz?
entities.description: Shiraz is a versatile red wine grape known as Syrah internationally. Learn what Shiraz tastes like, whether it is sweet and how Australian regions shape its style.

entities.name: What is Susumaniello?
entities.description: Susumaniello is a dark-skinned Italian wine grape associated with Puglia, Brindisi and Salento. Learn what its red and rosé wines can taste like, how it is used in blends, and how Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What is Sylvaner?
entities.description: Sylvaner is a white wine grape known as Silvaner in Germany. Learn where it is grown, how it tastes, the styles it makes and how Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What Is Tempranillo?
entities.description: Tempranillo is a Spanish red grape that can make juicy young wines or complex oak-aged styles. Learn what Australian drinkers should expect.

entities.name: What is Teroldego?
entities.description: Teroldego is a red grape from Trentino known for deeply coloured, fresh and structured wines. Learn its origins, style, Australian context and serving tips.

entities.name: What is Timorasso?
entities.description: Timorasso is an Italian white grape from Piedmont known for dry, textured wines with fresh acidity and the ability to develop savoury complexity with age. Learn what the grape is, what its label terms mean and where Australian drinkers may encounter it.

entities.name: What is Tinta Barroca?
entities.description: Tinta Barroca is a Portuguese grape associated with the Douro. Learn how it is grown, what it contributes to Douro wines and Port blends, and what Australian drinkers may encounter.

entities.name: What is Tintilia?
entities.description: Tintilia is an Italian red wine grape associated with Molise. Learn how Tintilia differs from Tintilia del Molise, what its wines can taste like and how the grape may appear in Australia.

entities.name: What is Trepat?
entities.description: Trepat is a Catalan red wine grape associated with Conca de Barberà and used for fresh reds, rosés and rosé Cava. Learn what it tastes like and how to read the label.

entities.name: What is Trousseau?
entities.description: Trousseau is a red grape from eastern France, best known in the Jura and also encountered as Bastardo, Merenzao and Maturana Tinta. Learn what its wines taste like, why styles vary and where it appears in Australia.

entities.name: What is Verdejo?
entities.description: Verdejo is a Spanish white wine grape best known for fresh, aromatic wines from Rueda. Learn what Verdejo tastes like, how it differs from Rueda and how to serve it.

entities.name: What is Vinhão?

entities.name: Yecla

entities.name: What Is Acid Adjustment?
entities.description: Acid adjustment is a measured winemaking intervention that can change a wine’s balance, freshness and stability. Learn how it differs from acidity, pH and titratable acidity.

entities.name: Alcoholic fermentation in wine
entities.description: Learn how yeast converts grape sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide, how winemakers manage fermentation, and why the process affects wine style.

entities.name: What Is Amphora and Clay Vessels?
entities.description: Learn what amphora and clay vessels are, how winemakers use them, how they may affect wine and why amphora does not automatically mean natural or better wine.

entities.name: What Is Ancestral-Method Sparkling Wine Production?
entities.description: Ancestral-method sparkling wine finishes its original fermentation in the bottle. Learn how it works, why it is linked with pét-nat, and how it differs from traditional and tank methods.

entities.name: What Is Appassimento?
entities.description: Appassimento is a grape-drying technique that concentrates sugar and flavour. Learn how it works, whether the wine is sweet and how to read the term on an Australian label.

entities.name: What Is Barrel Ageing?
entities.description: Barrel ageing is wine maturation in a wooden barrel, usually oak. Learn how wood, oxygen, barrel size and previous use can influence wine.

entities.name: What Is Blending Wine?
entities.description: Learn what wine blending is, why winemakers combine separate lots, how blend trials work, and how blending differs from co-fermentation, field blends and finished wine blends.

entities.name: What Is Botrytis and Noble Rot?
entities.description: Learn what Botrytis cinerea does to wine grapes, how noble rot differs from destructive grey rot, and why it can produce concentrated sweet wines.

entities.name: What Is Bottle Ageing?
entities.description: Bottle ageing is how wine develops after bottling. Learn what changes in a sealed bottle, how oxygen, closures and storage matter, and why older does not always mean better.

entities.name: What Is Cap Management?
entities.description: Cap management is the handling of grape skins, seeds and other solids that rise during red-wine fermentation. Learn how punch-downs and pump-overs influence contact, extraction, colour, tannin and temperature.

entities.name: What Is Carbon Dioxide in Wine?
entities.description: Carbon dioxide in wine explained simply: how fermentation creates CO₂, why still wine can have spritz, how sparkling wine retains bubbles and what CO₂ does to texture and aroma.

entities.name: Carbonic maceration
entities.description: Carbonic maceration uses intact grapes in a carbon-dioxide-rich, oxygen-limited environment. Learn how it differs from semi-carbonic and whole-bunch fermentation, and what it may contribute to Australian wine.

entities.name: What Is Chaptalisation?
entities.description: Chaptalisation is the addition of fermentable sugar to grape must before or during fermentation. Learn how it affects potential alcohol, why it does not necessarily make wine sweet, and how Australia’s rules require careful qualification.

entities.name: What Is Co-fermentation?
entities.description: Co-fermentation explained in plain English: what it means, how it differs from blending, why winemakers use it and what it can change in wine.

entities.name: What Is Cold Stabilisation?
entities.description: Cold stabilisation chills wine before bottling to reduce the risk of tartrate crystals forming later. Learn how it works, why crystals are usually harmless and how it differs from cold soak, filtration and fining.

entities.name: What Are Concrete Eggs and Tanks?
entities.description: Learn what concrete eggs and tanks do in winemaking, how they differ from stainless steel, oak and clay, and what “made in concrete” really tells you.

entities.name: What Is Cultured Yeast Fermentation?
entities.description: Cultured yeast fermentation explained simply: how deliberate yeast inoculation works, why winemakers use it and how it differs from native fermentation.

entities.name: What Is Dealcoholised Wine Production?
entities.description: Learn how dealcoholised wine is made from fermented wine, including membrane, vacuum and spinning-cone processes, sensory changes and Australian labelling context.

entities.name: Destemming and crushing in winemaking
entities.description: Destemming removes grape stems; crushing breaks berries to release juice. Learn how these related operations shape must, solids, tannin, extraction and fermentation choices in Australian winemaking.

entities.name: What Is Direct-press rosé?
entities.description: Direct-press rosé is made by pressing red grapes early and fermenting the juice separately. Learn how it differs from saignée and affects colour.

entities.name: What Is Extended Maceration?
entities.description: Extended maceration means prolonged contact between red wine and grape solids. Learn how it can affect tannin, colour, texture and structure, and how it differs from cold soak and carbonic maceration.

entities.name: What Is Fermentation Temperature?
entities.description: Fermentation temperature affects yeast activity, fermentation speed, aroma, colour and extraction. Learn why red, white and rosé wines may use different strategies.

entities.name: What Is Filtering Wine?
entities.description: Learn what wine filtration is, why winemakers use it, how depth, cross-flow and membrane filtration differ, and what “filtered” and “unfiltered” mean in Australia.

entities.name: What Is Fining Wine?
entities.description: Fining is a winemaking treatment used to clarify wine and adjust selected compounds. Learn how it differs from filtering, what “unfined” means and how fining relates to vegan wine in Australia.

entities.name: What Is Flor Ageing?
entities.description: Learn what flor ageing is, how a living surface yeast film changes wine, which Sherry styles use flor, and how it differs from oxidation, lees and solera ageing.

entities.name: What Is Fortification?
entities.description: Learn what fortification means in winemaking, when spirit is added, how timing affects sweetness and alcohol, and what Australian fortified-wine terms mean.

entities.name: What Is French Oak vs American Oak?
entities.description: Learn how French oak and American oak differ in wine, including species, aroma tendencies, toast, barrel age and Australian usage.

entities.name: Hand-picked vs machine-harvested grapes
entities.description: Understand how hand-picked and machine-harvested grapes differ, why Australian vineyards may use either method, and why harvesting method alone does not determine wine quality.

entities.name: How alcohol is removed from wine
entities.description: Learn how alcohol is removed from fermented wine using vacuum, distillation, spinning-cone and membrane methods, and why aroma, flavour and body can change.

entities.name: How bushfires affect wine
entities.description: Learn how bushfire smoke, heat, fire damage and vineyard disruption can affect grapes and wine—and why smoke exposure is not automatically smoke taint.

entities.name: How Climate Affects Wine
entities.description: Learn how temperature, sunlight, rainfall and seasonal conditions influence grape ripeness, acidity, flavour and wine style.

entities.name: How frost affects vineyards
entities.description: Learn how frost damages grapevines, why spring frost after budburst is risky, how Australian vineyard sites differ, and how growers monitor and manage frost.

entities.name: How grapes are harvested
entities.description: Learn how wine grapes are harvested, how growers decide when to pick, and the practical differences between hand and machine harvesting in Australia.

entities.name: How hail affects vineyards
entities.description: Learn how hail can damage vineyard leaves, shoots, flowers, bunches and berries, why timing matters, and how one localised storm may affect both the current crop and future vine health.

entities.name: How low-alcohol wine is made
entities.description: Learn how low-alcohol wine is made through grape and fermentation choices, blending or post-fermentation alcohol removal, including reverse osmosis, vacuum distillation and spinning-cone processing.

entities.name: How non-alcoholic wine is made
entities.description: Most dealcoholised wine starts as fermented wine. Learn how alcohol is removed, why aroma and texture can change, and what Australian labels may mean.

entities.name: How Soil Affects Wine
entities.description: Soil can influence wine through water availability, root growth, nutrients and vine development—but it does not simply transfer its flavour to grapes. Learn how soil, climate and winemaking interact.

entities.name: How to choose wine in a bottle shop
entities.description: Choosing wine in a bottle shop is easier when you decide what you want before you study the shelf. Start with the occasion, food, budget and one or two…

entities.name: How to compare two bottles of wine
entities.description: A practical guide to comparing two bottles of wine fairly, from label information and tasting conditions to preference, value, suitability and possible faults.

entities.name: How to open an old bottle of wine
entities.description: Learn how to open an older bottle carefully, choose between a standard corkscrew and an Ah-So, manage fragile or broken corks, pour around sediment and decide whether decanting is worthwhile.

entities.name: How Wine Is Made
entities.description: How wine is made, from grape harvest and fermentation to maturation, blending and bottling. Learn how red, white, rosé, sparkling and fortified wines take different paths, and how yeast, skins, oak, lees and other winemaking choices influence the finished style.

entities.name: What Is Icewine Production?
entities.description: Learn how Icewine is made from naturally frozen grapes, why pressing frozen fruit concentrates the juice, and how the process differs from other sweet-wine methods.

entities.name: What Is Late-harvest Winemaking?
entities.description: Learn how late-harvest winemaking changes grape ripeness, sugar, acidity and fermentation—and why late harvest does not automatically mean sweet wine.

entities.name: What Is Lees ageing?
entities.description: Lees ageing explained simply: what lees are, how contact affects wine, why lees stirring is optional, and how to recognise terms such as “on lees” and “sur lie”.

entities.name: What Is Lees Stirring?
entities.description: Lees stirring, also called bâtonnage, is the deliberate resuspension of wine sediment. Learn how it differs from lees ageing and how it may affect texture, integration and oxygen exposure.

entities.name: What Is Micro-oxygenation?
entities.description: Micro-oxygenation is controlled oxygen exposure used in winemaking. Learn how it differs from aeration, oxidation and barrel ageing, and why it may affect tannins, colour and texture.

entities.name: What Is Native Yeast Fermentation?
entities.description: Native yeast fermentation explained: how it differs from cultured yeast, what “wild” and “spontaneous” mean, possible benefits and risks, and what Australian wine drinkers should know.

entities.name: What Is New Oak vs Old Oak?
entities.description: Understand the difference between new, first-fill, used, old and neutral oak, including flavour, maturation and practical tasting clues.

entities.name: What Are Oak Toast Levels?
entities.description: Oak toast level explained in plain English: how barrel heating changes oak, what light to heavy toast may suggest, and why toast is only one part of wine’s oak character.

entities.name: Pressing wine grapes
entities.description: Pressing separates juice or wine from grape solids. Learn how it differs from crushing, when it occurs in white, rosé and red winemaking, and how pressure affects wine style.

entities.name: What Are Punch-downs and Pump-overs?
entities.description: Learn how punch-downs and pump-overs manage the cap during red-wine fermentation, and how each technique can influence extraction, temperature, oxygen exposure and wine texture.

entities.name: What Is Racking Wine?
entities.description: Learn what racking wine means, why winemakers rack wine off the lees, how it relates to clarification and oxygen exposure, and why it differs from filtering, fining and decanting.

entities.name: What Is Reverse Osmosis in Winemaking?
entities.description: Reverse osmosis in winemaking explained simply: how membranes, permeate and retentate work, why producers use the process, its limitations and Australian context.

entities.name: What Is Saignée Method?
entities.description: Learn what the saignée method is, how draining juice from a red ferment can produce rosé, and why its effects on red-wine style are variable.

entities.name: What Is Semi-carbonic Maceration?
entities.description: Learn what semi-carbonic maceration means, how intact grapes and yeast fermentation work together, and how the process differs from carbonic maceration and whole-bunch fermentation.

entities.name: What Is Skin Contact in White Wine?
entities.description: Skin contact in white wine explained simply: how it works, when it happens, what it can do to colour and texture, and how it relates to orange wine in Australia.

entities.name: What Is Solera Ageing?
entities.description: Solera ageing explained simply: how criaderas and the oldest tier work, why solera wines contain multiple ages, and what Australian drinkers should know about fortified-wine terminology.

entities.name: What Is Stainless-Steel Winemaking?
entities.description: Learn what stainless-steel winemaking means, why tanks are used for fermentation and storage, how steel affects oxygen and temperature management, and why “unoaked” does not always mean stainless steel.

entities.name: What Is Sulfur dioxide in wine?
entities.description: Learn what sulphur dioxide and sulphites do in wine, why winemakers use them, how naturally occurring and added sulphites differ, and what “contains sulphites” means in Australia.

entities.name: What Is Tank-Method Sparkling Wine Production?
entities.description: Learn how tank-method sparkling wine is made, why it is also called Charmat or Martinotti, how it differs from traditional and ancestral methods, and why it is associated with—but not the same as—Prosecco.

entities.name: What Are Tartrate Crystals?
entities.description: Tartrate crystals are harmless wine deposits often formed from potassium bitartrate. Learn why they appear, how cold storage affects them, and how to serve wine containing crystals.

entities.name: What Is Traditional-method Sparkling Wine Production?
entities.description: Learn how traditional-method sparkling wine is made, from base wine and tirage to bottle fermentation, lees ageing, riddling, disgorgement and dosage—with Australian label context.

entities.name: What Are Wine Grape Clones?
entities.description: Wine grape clones are selected vine lines within a grape variety. Learn how clones differ from varieties and rootstocks, why growers use them and what they can—and cannot—tell you about wine style.

entities.name: What Does Oak Do to Wine?
entities.description: Learn how oak can influence wine flavour, aroma, texture and ageing, and why not every oaked wine tastes the same.

entities.name: What Does Yeast Do in Wine?
entities.description: Yeast turns grape sugar into alcohol, carbon dioxide and heat during fermentation. Learn how yeast affects wine aroma, texture and style.

entities.name: What does estate bottled mean?
entities.description: Learn what “estate bottled” means on a wine label, how the term differs between the United States and Australia, and what it does—and does not—tell you about provenance.

entities.name: What is a solera system?
entities.description: A plain-language guide to solera ageing: how wine moves through criaderas, why producers use the system, and what “solera” does—and does not—tell you about age.

entities.name: What is acidification in wine?
entities.description: Acidification is the controlled addition of acid to grape juice, must or wine. Learn why winemakers use it, how pH differs from titratable acidity, and how it differs from malolactic fermentation and deacidification.

entities.name: What is autolysis in sparkling wine?
entities.description: Autolysis is the gradual breakdown of spent yeast cells during lees ageing. Learn how it shapes sparkling wine’s aroma, texture and foam, and why more time on lees does not guarantee one flavour.

entities.name: What is botrytis in wine grapes?
entities.description: Botrytis in wine grapes can cause damaging grey mould or, under particular drying conditions, desirable noble rot. Learn how *Botrytis cinerea* affects grapes and wine.

entities.name: What is canopy management?
entities.description: A plain-English guide to canopy management: what it means, why growers manage vine growth, the main techniques, Australian conditions and the trade-offs between dense and exposed canopies.

entities.name: What Is Cold Soak in Winemaking?
entities.description: Cold soak is a cool, pre-fermentation period of skin contact used mainly in red-wine production. Learn how it may influence colour, aroma, flavour and tannin.

entities.name: What is cover cropping in vineyards?
entities.description: Cover cropping means growing or managing plants around grapevines. Learn why vineyards use it, its benefits and trade-offs, and why Australian conditions matter.

entities.name: What is crop thinning?
entities.description: Crop thinning is the deliberate removal of grape bunches or other fruit-bearing material to manage crop load. Learn why timing, vine balance and Australian vineyard conditions matter—and why it does not guarantee better wine.

entities.name: What is deacidification in wine?
entities.description: Deacidification is the controlled reduction of excessive acidity in wine. Learn how biological conversion, blending and technical treatments can change a wine’s acid balance, and why pH is not the same as titratable acidity.

entities.name: What is délestage?
entities.description: Délestage, also called rack-and-return, separates fermenting red-wine juice from grape solids before returning it over the cap. Learn how it differs from pump-overs and punch-downs.

entities.name: What is disgorgement in sparkling wine?
entities.description: Disgorgement is the removal of sediment from a sparkling-wine bottle after traditional-method secondary fermentation and lees ageing. Learn how it differs from riddling and dosage.

entities.name: What is dosage in sparkling wine?
entities.description: Dosage is the finishing addition made to sparkling wine after disgorgement. Learn what it contains, how it affects sweetness and balance, and why it is not a quality scale.

entities.name: What is dry farming in vineyards?
entities.description: Dry farming means growing grapevines without routine irrigation. Learn how rainfall, soil moisture and site conditions affect vines, grapes and Australian vineyards.

entities.name: What Is Fermentation in Wine?
entities.description: Fermentation is the process in which yeast converts grape sugar into alcohol, carbon dioxide and flavour compounds. Learn how it shapes wine.

entities.name: What is flor ageing?
entities.description: Flor ageing is wine matured beneath a living film of yeast. Learn how flor works, how it changes wine and why it is associated with Fino and Manzanilla.

entities.name: What is fractional blending?
entities.description: Fractional blending repeatedly removes part of a wine and replaces it with younger or different wine. Learn how it works, why producers use it and how it differs from ordinary blending and solera ageing.

entities.name: What is free-run juice?
entities.description: Free-run juice is the grape juice that drains naturally before stronger pressing. Learn how it differs from press juice and why wineries may separate or blend the fractions.

entities.name: What is grape must?
entities.description: Grape must is the grape material that becomes wine. Learn how must differs from juice and wine, what it can contain, and why skins, seeds and fermentation matter.

entities.name: What is green harvesting?
entities.description: Green harvesting is the deliberate removal of immature grape bunches before harvest. Learn why growers use it, when it happens and why it does not guarantee better wine.

entities.name: What is icewine?
entities.description: Icewine is a sweet wine made from grapes that freeze naturally on the vine and are harvested and pressed while frozen. Learn how frozen pressing concentrates the juice and how icewine differs from other sweet wines.

entities.name: What is irrigation in vineyards?
entities.description: Vineyard irrigation explained in plain English: why growers use it, how rainfall and soil moisture affect vines, and what irrigation can mean for grapes and wine.

entities.name: What is late-harvest wine?
entities.description: Learn how late-harvest wine is made, why grapes are left on the vine longer, how this affects sweetness and flavour, and why it is different from Icewine.

entities.name: What Is Malolactic Fermentation?
entities.description: Malolactic fermentation is a bacterial conversion that changes malic acid into lactic acid. Learn how it affects acidity, texture and aroma, why winemakers manage it, and why it matters in Australian red wine and Chardonnay.

entities.name: What is noble rot?
entities.description: Noble rot is a beneficial form of *Botrytis cinerea* infection that concentrates ripe grapes. Learn how it differs from harmful rot, late harvest and Icewine.

entities.name: What is press wine?
entities.description: Press wine is the liquid extracted from grape skins, seeds and other solids during pressing. Learn how it differs from free-run wine and how winemakers use it.

entities.name: What is reverse osmosis in winemaking?
entities.description: Reverse osmosis in winemaking explained in plain English: how pressure and a semipermeable membrane create permeate and retentate, and why wineries may use the process.

entities.name: What is riddling in sparkling wine?
entities.description: Riddling is the process of gradually rotating and tilting a bottle so sparkling-wine sediment collects in the neck before disgorgement. Learn how it works and where it fits in traditional-method production.

entities.name: What is spinning cone technology?
entities.description: Spinning cone technology uses rotating cones, thin liquid films, gas flow and reduced pressure to manage wine aroma and alcohol. Learn how it works, where it is used and why the result can differ from the original wine.

entities.name: What Is Terroir?
entities.description: Terroir describes how place, climate, site, soil, vine and people interact to shape wine. Learn what the term usefully means.

entities.name: What is tirage in sparkling wine?
entities.description: Tirage is the step that prepares traditional-method sparkling wine for its second fermentation. Learn how it differs from dosage and creates bottle-fermented bubbles.

entities.name: What is vine yield?
entities.description: Vine yield is the amount of grapes produced by a vine or vineyard area. Learn how kg/vine, tonnes per hectare, crop load and vine balance differ—and why low yield is not automatically better.

entities.name: What unfiltered wine means
entities.description: Unfiltered wine is bottled without a final filtration step, but it may still be clarified. Learn what the term means for haze, sediment, taste, stability and serving in Australia.

entities.name: When to stand an old bottle upright
entities.description: Learn when standing an old wine bottle upright helps settle sediment, how long to leave it, and how to serve it carefully at home.

entities.name: What Is Whole-Berry Fermentation?
entities.description: Learn what whole-berry fermentation means, how it differs from whole-bunch and carbonic maceration, and how intact berries can influence wine’s texture, aroma and extraction.

entities.name: What Is Whole-Bunch Fermentation?
entities.description: Whole-bunch fermentation retains some or all grape bunches, including stems, during red-wine fermentation. Learn how it works, how it differs from carbonic maceration, and how it can affect wine.

entities.name: Wine bottle sizes explained
entities.description: Understand common wine bottle capacities, traditional format names and what Australian shoppers should read on the label.
